questions.q: How does a hunting query differ from a scheduled analytics rule?
options: It isn't scheduled and doesn't alert on its own — an analyst runs it manually, on demand
It can only be run inside the hunting query gallery, never written from scratch
It raises an incident's severity automatically
It is the same thing as an analytics rule, just with a different name
questions.explain: A hunting query is KQL an analyst runs manually to look for something that hasn't already triggered an automated detection, unlike a scheduled analytics rule.

questions.q: Why can't an analytics rule catch the slow data exfiltration example from this lesson?
options: The transfer stays just under every threshold a correlation rule checks for, so nothing ever fires
Analytics rules can only run on a weekly schedule
Data exfiltration never produces any log data at all
Analytics rules are disabled whenever a hunting query is active
questions.explain: Because nothing about the slow exfiltration crosses a configured threshold, no analytics rule ever fires on it — only an actively run hunting query can surface it.

questions.q: What does Sentinel's hunting query gallery provide?
options: A built-in library of pre-built KQL hunting queries organized by attack tactic, maintained by Microsoft
A list of every incident currently assigned to an analyst
A record of every custom analytics rule an organization has written
A billing dashboard for data ingestion costs
questions.explain: The gallery is a genuine starting point for hunting, organized by tactics like credential access and lateral movement, without requiring an analyst to write KQL from scratch.

questions.q: Why does a maturing hunting program also write custom hunting queries beyond the gallery?
options: The gallery can't anticipate every environment's own specific risk
Custom queries are required before the gallery can be used at all
Gallery queries stop working after 30 days
Custom queries automatically become scheduled analytics rules
questions.explain: A maturing program writes custom hunting queries targeted at patterns specific to its own organization that no pre-built gallery query covers.

questions.q: What happens when a hunt turns up genuinely suspicious activity?
options: The analyst can pivot into a full investigation, and the pattern can be turned into a new scheduled analytics rule going forward
The hunting query is automatically deleted from the workspace
Nothing — hunting results cannot be acted on directly
The finding is only visible to the analyst who ran the query, with no way to share it
questions.explain: A real hunt result can lead straight into an investigation and, if worth catching automatically, become a new rule — the continuous-improvement practice from the maturity model in action.
